I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code written by coding agents - here's a description of the external sandbox pattern, where agents run on your Mac but execute code in a WebAssembly or QEMU or Apple Container sandbox - with demos for Claude Code, Codex and Pi https://blog.primeradiant.com/external-sandboxes-for-coding-agents/

I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers - here's our index repository for these external sandbox prototypes https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/external-sandbox

Each of the three sandbox servers includes an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code can communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent

A lot of folks don't realize how much of our computer infrastructure is an improvised system prone to cascading failures. You didn't need offensive AI cyberattacks to have big outages like Microsoft/FAA. Of course, now we DO have to deal with offensive AI (but also defensive AIs)

I say this as I see every outage of the last five days get picked up by people who did not pay attention to cybersecurity before, usually with the implication that "this is the big one," which, in turn, leads people on both X and real life to panic and spread further rumors.

I will say that the Mythos security freakout, much derided at the time, and the focus on first deploying cyber models with limited access from the Labs seems to have been an effective step in mitigating some of the downside cyber risk that would have otherwise happened from AI.

最近硅谷两大佬因为马斯克吵翻了，结果老马亲自下场，一句话把全网看乐了。 先是著名反垄断评论家 Matt 泼冷水：SpaceX 算什么奇迹？马斯克根本不是天才，无非是会找华尔街搞钱，用钞票和工程师硬堆出来的。 这话连平时谁都不服的硅谷传奇程序员 DHH 都看不下去了，直接回怼：太酸了！哪怕你不喜欢马斯克，也得承认他“把吹过的牛变成现实”的能力举世无双。从特斯拉、脑机接口到 SpaceX，世上有一百万个会搞钱的投资人，但只有一个马斯克。 随后马斯克本尊下场，只回了一句灵魂反问：“行，那你给我解释一下蓝色起源、波音和 ULA？” 这一刀，直接捅在了“唯金钱论”的肺管子上。 如果光靠砸钱就能上天，那现在的太空霸主绝不可能是 SpaceX： 1、 比谁更有钱？ 贝索斯的蓝色起源比 SpaceX 早成立两年，背后站着前世界首富，从来不缺钱，结果到现在还在努力追赶。 2、 比谁补贴多？ NASA 当年搞载人航天，同一个任务，给波音砸了 42 亿美元，给 SpaceX 只给了 26 亿。结果 SpaceX 从 2020 年就开始像公交车一样送宇航员上天，波音的飞船却连宇航员都接不回来，最后还得靠 SpaceX 去救场。 3、 比华尔街输血？ SpaceX 起步根本没有华尔街一分钱，全是马斯克卖掉 PayPal 后自己掏的 1 亿美元家底。猎鹰 1 号连炸三次后差点破产，第四次才绝处逢生。 DHH 说得太对了：钱能买来顶级工程师，但买不来“不怕炸火箭”的魄力。 看看星舰第 15 次试飞（Flight 15）就懂了：同一个任务里，助推器在海里丢了，但飞船却从轨道返航、被发射塔的“机械筷子”稳稳夹住。 放在传统航天巨头那里，“丢了助推器”这半句话，就够他们停飞开两年的事故批斗会了；但在 SpaceX，这只是通往成功的又一组实验数据。 @elonmusk 说实话，到底哪个更难造：是一枚能上天的火箭，还是一家“允许工程师靠炸火箭来试错”的公司？ Let’s take this gentleman’s argument at face value that anyone can throw money at rockets and get something like Starship, Falcon or Dragon. Great practical paper from Google on building efficient agent skills. For cheaper agents, learn a skill for accuracy first, then prune it for length. This has also worked well in our own experiments. Skill optimizers usually add a new rule after every failure. The skill grows, the agent reads more tokens every turn, and long loops start to time out. EfficientSkill runs two phases. The first repairs failures with no length penalty until the skill reaches a target accuracy. The second prunes instructions and moves reusable code into workspace utilities, while accuracy has to stay close to that target. Pruning from the empty seed stalls, so the order matters. Across four models on MATH-500, ALFWorld, and SpreadsheetBench, output tokens fall on 11 of 12 configurations, up to 80% of the time. Accuracy also rises on every benchmark, including +14.3 points with Gemini 3.8 Flash and +17.5 points with Grok 4.1 Fast on SpreadsheetBench. Serving cost drops 25% to 67%. https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19823 Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/efficientskill-learning-skills-for-token-efficient-multi-turn-agents-2611.19823

Banger paper from Google on RSI. (bookmark it) They propose an approach for continual recursive self-improvement at the harness level. They also propose their own self-improving memory system for the harness optimizer. This clearly highlights the importance of traces and having a functional, adaptive, and structured persistent memory system in your harness. They show that a harness optimizer improves 9 of 10 continued runs when it remembers why it made each past edit. They discuss that a common problem shows up when you change the model or the benchmark. An Opus-evolved harness started at 68.41 on Gemini, below the 73.89 of the plain seed harness. Self-Improvement Memory groups past edits by the harness problem they addressed. For each edit, it stores the rationale, predicted outcome, observed outcome, and evaluation context. The proposer and the selector both read it before making new changes. Across four domains, including Terminal-Bench 2.1 to Terminal-Bench 4, SIM beats continuing from the harness alone in six cross-dataset and four Opus-to-Gemini settings. Across ten coding runs, it adds 2.36 points on average (p=0.003). If you evolve harnesses automatically, store the reasons and results of each edit next to the code. https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18856 Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/self-improvement-memory-enables-continual-recursive-self-improvement-2611.18856

Could be the start of a trend in new pre-training recipes: no LR decay phase anymore. (Also seen in Kolibri.) Instead: constant LR + averaging the last N checkpoints (or a running weight average). I guess that makes it easier in practice because you don't have to commit to a total training length upfront. A little meta analysis based on those who share training details: - Classic cosine: Llama 3, OLMo 2, OLMo 3, GLM-4.5, GLM-5, Kimi K3, Phi-4 - WSD ("Warmup-Stable-Decay"): DeepSeek V3, DeepSeek V4, DeepSeek V4.1-Flash, Kimi K2, Kimi Linear, Nemotron 3 Nano, Nemotron 3 Super, SmolLM3, MiniMax M2 - No decay (constant LR plus checkpoint averaging): Kolibri-1, DatologyAI's models Trick #3: Merge, merge, merge. In pretraining, we skipped LR decay for a running weight average. Then we merged pre-context-extension models into post-extension checkpoints (see fig. for ablation study gains). Merging was also an expedient stand-in for MOPD in our RLVR recipe.

devin bots are multi-agent teams done right: - always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI) - own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others) - manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself) - available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction) - consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212) this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god) hyped concepts this replaces: - /goal - "ultracode" / "ultra mode" - "loop engineering" - "agent to agent" - "agent swarms" - AI employees (see below) my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes. incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol. if youre a startup, reminder that Devin for Startups offers 65k in credits. apply via clanker Meet Devin Bots. I've been following @Cloudflare since it began 17 yrs ago. Its latest move into creating System One models is fascinating, and when I sat down with @michellechen at @aiDotEngineer Code, I discovered there are more models to come — incl reasoning models! https://latent.space/p/cloudflare/

i kept getting questions on how we released clef so quickly after jev, but i strongly believe that we’re mostly reaping the benefits of asymmetric effort: new ideas are difficult to invent and easy to copy. @typesafeai has done an incredible job in pioneering this concept of system one models. i also strongly believe that it is not a zero-sum game! it’s almost a duty for all of us to solve difficult hardware constraints through software, and system one models allow us to offload some of the work we’d regularly send to LLMs towards smaller, faster, and less compute-intensive models. we’re also still challenging ourselves to invent in this space as well, with the launch of clairic and more. i’m excited for the future of cloudflare as a neolab and hope you are too. thank you to @ricmac for sitting down with me on this story! An illustration of both the power and issues with Astra 6.2 in a way that might be accessible: I asked it to create a game in Blender and Unity where you are the pilot of a Coast Guard cutter who travelled back in time to the War of Independence to stop the British invasion of New York. It made incredible 3D models and a working game with no errors - its even fun to play! But Astra got obsessed with random ideas that didn't make a lot of sense and built them out without asking along with following my instructions: you could put down false buoys to lure the ship in the wrong direction (like the British would understand a modern buoy?) or you could persuade the British ships to go the wrong direction by talking to them, or that you would spend your time rescuing sailors from other parts of the harbor. It didn't even initially have a shooting mechanism until I pointed it out. This is all kind of minor stuff individually, but it was frustrating to have the AI constantly do its own things without telling me, given its instincts were often off, and then have to redirect it constantly. Other models, including GPT-6 Asta, didn't require the same struggle to control and operate. And these same issues show up in academic research and other more serious use cases. Media
